- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.67), especially in early forecast periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or near zero, particularly after recent highs.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment shifts; model should not overshoot 1–2 days after sentiment turns negative.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming momentum; if sentiment is weak or mixed, cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 14-day high.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, allow slight upward bias but cap at 5% above prior 7-day high.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral, reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior 7-day average, especially if recent price action shows downward momentum.
